title: StudioDash Reporting
description: Review historical performance, compare reporting periods, analyse revenue and app trends, and understand how your studio is changing with StudioDash.
summary: StudioDash reporting helps you move beyond isolated metrics by showing how apps, revenue, websites, providers, and business performance change over time.
heroImageAlt: StudioDash reporting and performance analytics dashboard

referenceImage.alt: StudioDash reporting and performance analytics dashboard

featureShowcases.heading: Understand What Changed
featureShowcases.summary: Review performance over time and identify the apps, revenue sources, and services behind the changes you see.
featureShowcases.body: StudioDash turns information collected from your connected services into a clearer historical view of your studio. Compare different periods, explore revenue and app performance, and move from high-level trends into the detail behind them without rebuilding reports manually.
bullets: Review historical performance across your portfolio.
Compare results over different reporting periods.
Explore revenue by app, source, country, and date where available.
Use connected data to understand the context behind changes.

image.alt: StudioDash reporting view showing revenue trends and historical performance
image.caption: Explore how your apps and studio are performing over time.

sections.heading: Put Today's Numbers into Context
paragraphs: A single number only tells you what happened at one point in time. StudioDash reporting helps you understand whether that result is part of a longer trend, a short-term change, or something affecting a particular app or provider.
By keeping historical information from supported services available, StudioDash makes it easier to compare performance without repeatedly collecting and combining reports from different platforms.

sections.heading: Compare Different Reporting Periods
paragraphs: StudioDash lets you review information over different periods so you can look at recent activity as well as longer-term performance.
Changing the reporting period helps reveal whether revenue, downloads, website activity, or other metrics are moving in a meaningful direction rather than reacting to a single day's result.
bullets: See whether changes are temporary or sustained.
Use historical context when making development or business decisions.

sections.heading: Explore Revenue in More Detail
paragraphs: Revenue is one of the areas where combined reporting can provide the most value. StudioDash brings supported revenue information together and lets you explore how different apps and sources contribute to the overall result.

Where the connected provider supplies the information, reporting can include breakdowns by source, app, date, and country, helping you investigate the changes behind a total rather than seeing only a single figure.
bullets: Explore country and date breakdowns where available.
See revised provider figures as updated data becomes available.

sections.heading: Measure Progress Against Your Goals
paragraphs: StudioDash can put revenue into the context of the business goals you set for your studio. This makes reporting more useful than simply showing whether a figure has gone up or down.
As goals change over time, your reporting can preserve that history, helping you understand performance against the targets that applied during each period.
bullets: Keep business targets visible alongside revenue.
Understand progress towards break-even or other goals.
Preserve the history of goal changes over time.
Give commercial performance more useful context.

sections.heading: Understand Performance Across Your Apps
paragraphs: For developers managing several products, portfolio reporting makes it easier to see which apps are contributing to growth and which may need attention.
App Store information, revenue, and other supported data can be viewed together so individual products are not judged from a single metric alone.

sections.heading: Include Website & Search Performance
paragraphs: StudioDash reporting is not limited to apps. Supported website analytics and search information can also be reviewed over time, helping you understand whether changes in visibility or website activity are part of a wider trend.
This keeps your website and app portfolio within the same reporting workflow rather than treating them as unrelated parts of the business.

sections.heading: Know When Provider Data Changes
paragraphs: External services do not all publish or finalise information in the same way. Some providers may revise recent figures after validation, while others only make certain reports available periodically.
StudioDash reporting reflects the latest supported information available from connected services, helping historical reporting remain useful when a provider updates previously reported figures.

sections.heading: Historical Data Without Rebuilding Every Report
paragraphs: StudioDash keeps useful previously collected information available so changing reporting periods does not require every provider to be contacted again.
This makes historical exploration faster and helps build a more consistent view of your studio over time.

sections.heading: Reporting That Grows with Your Plan
paragraphs: StudioDash is designed around Free, Pro, and Studio plans. Free provides a useful overview, while paid plans can provide access to more detailed reporting, breakdowns, and business-focused information.
This allows developers to start with the level of reporting they need and move to more advanced analysis as their portfolio or studio grows.

sections.heading: From Reporting to Better Decisions
paragraphs: StudioDash is continuing to expand beyond traditional reporting. Business intelligence and assistant capabilities are being developed to help interpret the information already collected and highlight areas that may deserve attention.
The aim is to reduce the time spent manually interpreting several dashboards and make StudioDash increasingly useful as a decision-making tool for independent developers and small studios.
